The air in the "Zen & Serenity" studio was thick with the scent of eucalyptus and suppressed judgment. Jim, a man whose idea of flexibility was reaching for the remote without standing up, had intended to join the "Intro to Chair Yoga" class next door. He had, however, walked into the "Advanced Inversions & Acrobatics" session.

The instructor, a woman named Seraphina who looked like she was born in a downward dog, clapped her hands once. The sound was like a gunshot in a library.

"Welcome, seekers," she whispered, her voice echoing off the hardwood floors. "Today, we explore the balance between stillness and the void. Please, assume the position of the Long-Necked Heron."

Jim looked around. Everyone else was standing on one leg, arms extended, looking like elegant, confused flamingos. Jim, panicking, decided to mimic the general vibe. He stood on his left leg, raised his right arm, and stretched his neck upward as far as it would go, trying to look serene.

"Good," Seraphina murmured, gliding past him. "Feel the stretch in your cervical spine. Let your body become a conduit for the universe."

Jim felt a conduit for something else entirely. The pressure of the advanced pose, combined with the questionable burrito he’d eaten for lunch, created a perfect storm in his lower abdomen. He tried to hold the pose, but his body betrayed him.

*Pfft.*

A small, high-pitched sound escaped him. It was not the sound of spiritual release. It was the sound of a deflating whoopee cushion.

The class froze. Ten pairs of eyes turned toward Jim. Seraphina paused mid-pose, her eyebrow twitching.

"Jim," she said, her voice dangerously calm. "Is that... part of the practice?"

"No!" Jim squeaked, his face turning the color of a ripe tomato. "It’s just... the universe is very loud today!"

He tried to recover by deepening his pose, but the effort caused another, louder sound. *BRRRRAAAP.*

This time, it wasn’t just a sound; it was a vibration. The woman next to him, a serious-looking accountant named Linda, slowly lowered her leg. "Jim," she said, "I think you’re breaking the zen."

"I’m trying!" Jim cried, sweat pouring down
